question: Separate Hermit's syscall-interception (instrumentation) cost from its deterministic-scheduling (sequentialization) cost, and compare both against native and FULL gVisor measured on the same host in the same core box.
supersedes: experiments/gvisor-systrap-benchmark-repro-20260802 (compared local Hermit against BLOG-PUBLISHED gVisor numbers from a different host; its own README retracts the resulting cross-host ordering)

method.instrumentation: exp1: single-threaded getpid, ALL arms in a K=1 core box; ns/syscall = median over 5 reps of (T(300k)-T(100k))/200k
method.why_a_slope: cancels fixed startup (process exec / Sentry boot / backend attach); a plain wall/N would have measured Sentry boot and reported gVisor ~100x worse
method.sequentialization: exp2: 4-thread getpid at N=200000, K=1 vs K=4, BOTH through the same core-box helper so its cost is common-mode, then the measured calibration median is subtracted from each side
method.core_box: scratch/run-on-k-free-cores.py — sched_setaffinity fallback (cpuset controller not delegated in this sandbox); picks the K least-busy free cores, never a fixed id

no_result.hermit-kvm: hangs on this host; rc=124 at a 45s probe and at the 300s bound; recorded as an explicit no-result, never a zero

environment.load_during_collection: 1-min load averaged roughly 50-83 across the run
environment.caveat: contended box; medians over 5 reps mitigate but do not remove this
